items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I remember being in the studio with Ron Carter and Jack DeJohnette and playing with those great musicians.

ctx.x: I know exactly what you’re saying. We had someone at Hamilton — I won’t mention names — but a working jazz musician who we were thinking that’s what we want to do. And he’s thinking, “I want your gig, I want to get a college gig and have that security and all that.” Whatever.

Right. Because the road gets tired and maybe playing — I’m telling you we’re at a crossroads in our culture now. I mean we have to really make a decision in terms of who we’re going to be and what we’re going to be and how we’re going to be and it’s out there. We really are there now. So somebody has to come forward, or certain people have to come forward and say this is really how it should be. And not necessarily for everybody but this is how it is for me, I still want to perform. I think, you know, the…

Before we actually started we were talking a little bit about how marketing is changing, has changed and will continue to change. You had a release that kind of sat around for a while, “Out of this World”?
